title: Takes, Hosts, Decoys, Strings & Lint
description: A motion verdict, one declaration on four hosts, a headline that lies to crawlers, pluckable underlines and a linter inside the page.

drops.title: Prove the Copy Moves the Same
drops.description: Two stages on one virtual clock, sampled every frame, aligned and scored until the rebuild matches the reference.
drops.concept: A reference motion and your rebuild run side by side on a shared virtual clock. Three elements per stage are sampled at 60fps, the copy is slid ±300 ms to find its best alignment, and the mean mismatch over the frames where either curve is actually moving decides the verdict — the same 80 ms / 2% tolerance a 'moves the same' check uses. Ghost trails show the last ten frames and the activity curves shade the difference in red.
drops.source: NiazMorshed2007/reanimate — record, spec, build, verify, repeat

interaction.mouse: Drag duration, delay and stagger and pick an easing to steer the copy toward the hidden reference.
interaction.click: ‘New reference take’ swaps in another hidden spec; the spec is revealed once you match it.
interaction.touch: All controls are sliders and a select; the panel stacks under the stages on narrow screens.

drops.title: One Declaration, Four Hosts
drops.description: One contract rendered as browser DOM, UIKit, AppKit and a framework-painted headerbar — unspecified tokens fall to each host.
drops.concept: A single declared screen — nav title, list, field, segmented control, toggle, primary button — is handed to four renderers. Because the contract names no colour, radius or type size, each host supplies its own: a browser toolbar, an iOS large title with inset rows and a tab bar, macOS traffic lights at 13px, a GTK-style headerbar the framework paints itself. Turning on the author layer makes all four converge, which is precedence author → platform → default expressed as stacked CSS custom-property scopes.
drops.source: expo/exact — declare once, render per host

interaction.mouse: Toggle the author layer, drag the authored radius, pick an accent and watch all four hosts converge.
interaction.click: Each host's segmented control, toggle and primary button are live; the hatch switch reveals the native escape hatch per host.
interaction.touch: The four hosts reflow to one column and every control is tappable.

drops.title: The Decoy Headline
drops.description: The markup ships a fluent decoy of every swapped word; the render layer puts the real one back, and a live scraper view shows the difference.
drops.concept: Word-level substitution with render-time reversal: each swapped word keeps its part of speech, so the decoy text reads as fluent prose, and the real word is restored as the page paints. A panel reads the DOM's own textContent back at you, so you can watch the other book being published while you read this one. The limits are stated rather than hidden — the codebook travels with the page, so what it buys is cost, not silence.
drops.source: isaqueseneda/shieldfont — word substitution reversed by the font's ccmp table (here the stylesheet is the codebook)

interaction.mouse: Hover any word to see the pair it belongs to, struck through in the direction that applies.
interaction.click: Switch off the shield to read the page as the markup spells it, underline the swapped words, or copy the decoy text.
interaction.touch: The density slider and both switches work by tap; the scraper view updates live.

drops.title: Underlines You Can Pluck
drops.description: Crossing a link plucks its underline — the displacement is decomposed into string modes with a fundamental set by the link's width.
drops.concept: The underline is a fixed-fixed string. Where you cross it sets the plucked position, your pointer speed sets the amplitude, and the triangular displacement is decomposed into the first modes of the string, each oscillating at its own multiple of the fundamental and decaying faster than the one below it. The fundamental is inversely proportional to the link's width, so a short word rings high and quick while a long phrase wobbles low — eight links of different lengths each sound their own note.

interaction.mouse: Cross or hover a link to pluck it; move faster for a bigger amplitude, cross near an end to favour the second mode.
interaction.click: Pressing a link plucks it hardest; the panel tunes tension, damping, amplitude and mode count, and can add a Web Audio pluck.
interaction.touch: Tapping a link plucks it, and the reduced-motion preference leaves every string at rest.

drops.title: The Linter Is a Component
drops.description: A linting overlay that measures the rendered page — clip boxes, intersections, hit-tests, contrast and tap targets — and pins every finding.
drops.concept: Most UI bugs only exist once the thing is rendered, so this component measures the render: text runs against their clip boxes, box intersections, an elementFromPoint hit-test for occlusion, WCAG 2 contrast against the first opaque ancestor background (and an honest 'unverifiable' for text on a gradient), tap-target minimums and placeholder values that leaked to the screen. Findings are numbered pins over the app under test, a clickable list and a terminal report with an exit code. A stress slider re-measures at any width from 320px up.
drops.source: ngocanhnckh/renderlint — lint the rendered UI, not the source

interaction.mouse: Drag the stress width, toggle longer text or bigger numbers, and the findings re-measure on the spot.
interaction.click: Click a pin or a row to select a finding; ‘Apply every fix’ drives the report to zero and ‘Reset’ puts the bugs back.
interaction.touch: Rule switches and the stress slider are tappable, and the report column stacks under the app.
